questions.q: For your own training script (not a built-in algorithm), how does a SageMaker tuning job learn each trial's objective metric?
options: A regular expression in metric_definitions extracts it from the training log
The script must upload it to S3 manually
SageMaker computes accuracy itself from the model file
It reads the metric from the hyperparameter dictionary
questions.explain: You give each metric a Name and a Regex; SageMaker applies the regex to the training job's log output and reads the value from the first capture group.

questions.q: Which tuning strategy supports only categorical hyperparameters and needs no max-jobs setting?
questions.explain: Grid search enumerates every combination of categorical values, so the number of training jobs is determined by the categories.

questions.q: Why is random search unaffected by running the maximum number of jobs in parallel?
options: It stops all jobs after the first result
It reuses the same hyperparameters for every job
Its choices do not depend on the results of earlier jobs
questions.explain: Random search draws each candidate independently of previous results, so parallelism costs nothing in search quality. Bayesian optimization, by contrast, learns from finished jobs.

questions.q: Which strategy is intended for iterative algorithms that report a metric after each epoch, such as neural networks?
questions.explain: Hyperband uses intermediate results to reallocate resources and stop underperforming jobs, so it needs an algorithm that publishes metrics at different resource levels.

questions.q: A learning rate could plausibly be anywhere from 0.0001 to 0.5. Which scaling type is the natural choice for that range?
questions.explain: A logarithmic scale samples evenly across orders of magnitude, which suits values such as learning rates that span several powers of ten.
